All seven files read. Here is the audit.

The packet under test is UP-130 (the request's key name says `packet_102_claim_valid`; no packet 102 appears in any file, so I treat the key as referring to the UP-130 claim). The fabrication audit rejects the UP-130 derivation decisively for its exact source hash, and the newer stage-interior receipts do not rescue it: PyTorch is locally red (seed-unstable Type-2 selection) and the JAX sweep verdict is fail (Type-2 ranking unstable with ties).

Signed up/down variants are Axis-6 placements of the same four maps, not new operators.",

Notes behind the verdict, briefly:

- The fabrication audit is internally consistent and load-bearing: its C3 finding is a logical identity (any word with exactly two A's and two B's has length 4), so gate 1 of the packet could never have failed. Its Bloch-angle and commutation findings I checked against the packet source directly: `leg_op` uses `expm(-1j*(pi/2)*sigma)`, which is `-i*sigma`, and conjugation kills the global phase, so the two "axes" commute — the packet's own C2 story cannot generate order structure.
- The newer receipts keep the separations you asked about clean. The JAX receipt encodes Type chirality (method placement) and Axis-6 (per-slot precedence) as separate inputs and shows the Axis-6 flip moves scores without swapping chirality. The README and the PyTorch `owner_substage_rule` both fix the four substages as the four base operators (Ti, Te, Fi, Fe per the signed-math packet), not candidate/measurement/gate/receipt.
- The two live readings on Type2_right — real engine-specific cycle versus margin noise — are both still admissible; neither receipt excludes one. The JSON holds that divergence in `next_discriminator` rather than picking a winner.
